newsitem.title: UK: UK's Brown - windfall tax priced in to share prices.
newsitem.headline: UK's Brown - windfall tax priced in to share prices.

text.p: Labour's finance spokesman Gordon Brown said on Tuesday that the planned windfall tax on privatised utilities was priced in to the relevant share prices even though he had not yet named exactly which companies will have to pay.
"I believe the levy is discounted in the share price already, that is what most analysts say," Brown told BBC television.

Asked how the tax could be discounted when he had yet to specify which utilities will have to pay the tax, Brown said: "People know that the privatised utilities who will be affected are those...regulated by statute."
"Only those companies who have made excess profits will pay the tax," he added.
Brown said he would undertake a detailed investigation of which companies have made excess profits. "I'll consult the regulators and listen to the representations of the companies."

Labour's windfall levy will pay for a three billion stg programme to get the young and long-term unemployed into work. Brown is thought to want to raise about five billion stg from the utilities in all.
